questions.learningObjective: Explain why one density unit is easier to read than the other
questions.stem: A translator's note asks why a density in grams per cubic centimetre is often easier to read than the same density in kilograms per cubic metre.

options.text: Because the grams per cubic centimetre value is the smaller number, and smaller numbers are easier to read.
Because grams per cubic centimetre is the more accurate unit for stating a density.
options.misconception: claims a unit choice changes the accuracy of a value

options.text: Because kilograms per cubic metre is only used for very large densities and nothing else.
options.misconception: restricts the bigger unit to a special case

options.text: Because grams per cubic centimetre can be converted without using the prefix kilo at all.
options.misconception: misses that the conversion still needs the prefix

questions.explanation: The same density is 2.7 g per cubic centimetre or 2700 kg per cubic metre, and the shorter number is easier to read. The units do not change the accuracy, and the conversion still uses the prefix.
questions.hint: Compare the numerical values in the two unit systems.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.learningObjective: Identify the extra information needed to quote a tip speed
questions.stem: A translator's note describes a fan blade turning at 300 revolutions per minute and asks how the note should express the blade's tip speed.

options.text: The tip speed should be quoted directly in revolutions per minute, since that is the blade's speed.
options.misconception: treats the rotation rate as the tip speed

options.text: The tip speed needs the blade radius, since a speed is a distance travelled divided by the time.
The tip speed can be read from the rotation rate alone, because the blade covers one circle each turn.
options.misconception: assumes a fixed blade size in the note

options.text: The tip speed is meaningless for a rotating body, because only straight-line motion has a speed.
options.misconception: claims a speed needs straight-line motion

questions.explanation: A speed is distance over time, so the tip speed needs the distance the tip covers each turn, which depends on the blade radius. The rotation rate gives no length at all.
questions.hint: A speed needs a distance, so find the tip's path.
